question: Explain overfitting, compare L2 regularization and early stopping, then summarize their advantages.
answer: Overfitting occurs when a model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen validation data, indicated by a large gap between training and validation accuracy [S1] [S4]. L2 regularization penalizes large weights to prevent overfitting, smoothing the model and keeping all features [S2] [S5]. It introduces a hyperparameter (lambda) that controls the strength of regularization [S2] [S5]. Early stopping monitors validation loss and stops training when it stops improving, saving compute and acting as an implicit regularizer [S1] [S3]. It requires a validation set and is sensitive to patience value [S3] [S5]. Dropout randomly zeroes units during training, preventing co-adaptation in neural networks [S3]. Dropout is mainly used for neural networks [S3]. Advantages of L2 regularization include its smoothness and compatibility with gradient-based optimizers [S2]. Dropout's main advantage is its ability to prevent co-adaptation in neural networks [S3]. Both methods are effective for reducing overfitting, with L2 regularization being smoother and more reproducible [S1] [S2] [S3] [S5].

Learning curves, which plot error against training set size, help diagnose whether a model suffers from high bias or high variance.

citations.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
citations.text:
1. Reading Learning Curves
A learning curve plots training error and validation error against the training set size. In a high-bias
model both errors are high and they converge close to each other; adding more data barely helps
because the model is too simple. In a high-variance model the training error is low and a large gap
separates it from the validation error; the validation error keeps falling as more data is added, so
collecting more data helps.
When a model is overfitting the first actions to try are a simpler model, stronger regularization,
more training data or early stopping.

citations.title: Ml Overfitting Mitigation Guide
citations.text:
L2 regularization and early stopping
3. Early stopping Early stopping monitors validation loss during training and stops when it has not
improved for a fixed number of epochs (the patience); the best checkpoint is restored. Advantages:
it needs no change to the model, saves training compute, and the stopping epoch acts as an
implicit regularizer. Disadvantages: it requires a held-out validation set that is then not used for
training, results are sensitive to the patience value, and noisy validation curves can trigger a
premature stop. 4. Dropout Dropout randomly zeroes a fraction p of hidden units at each training
step so units cannot co-adapt. It is applied only during training. It is mainly used for neural
networks.
